Generative Bionics plans a 5,000-square-meter Italian humanoid training hub with AMD

The first of three planned sites targets Q4 2027, linking real industrial practice with digital-twin simulation.

Humanoids Daily ↗21 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A proposed three-site network

Generative Bionics announced its Physical AI Data Factory plan on October 21. A 5,000-square-meter Italian hub targets Q4 2027, followed by another European site and a third serving global markets. The city, investment budget and timing of later facilities are not specified.

Real practice and simulation form a loop

The sites would recreate industrial settings for GENE.01 to collect vision, motion, force and tactile data. Digital twins would then vary objects and conditions before trained models return to physical robots for validation. The cycle aims to prepare robots before customer deployment.

AMD supplies the planned compute foundation

AMD Helios is intended for model training, physical and synthetic data processing and parallel simulations, without disclosed installation size or robot count. The accompanying image is a concept illustration. This remains planned infrastructure, not an operating facility or established industrial validation result.
